result.instructions:
Keeplight keeps the lights in this PC the way the user set them. OpenRGB does the hardware work; Keeplight keeps a setup per device and puts it back at sign-in, after sleep and when OpenRGB's devices change.

- get_devices lists every device with an id, its mode and color, whether Keeplight keeps it (kept, differs, changed or notKept), what it was kept as, and what probably lights it.
- A change is one action on one device: keep (what it shows now), keepDark (only when every light is off), putBack, stopKeeping (a Direct device is handed back to its own Onboard lighting), keepAsBefore (goes back to the setup before the last stopKeeping or setColor; on a kept device the two swap) or setColor with a color as #rrggbb, and optionally a zone id from get_devices to color only that zone (keeps the device's effect in the new color, or switches to Static or Direct; the color is kept). For a whole-PC color, plan one setColor per device.
- What get_devices reads comes from OpenRGB's record. After sleep, RAM can show its own rainbow while the record still says the kept color; putBack fixes that.

Rules:
- You may read anything at any time through the read tools. For "what went wrong", start with diagnose.
- Change nothing on your own initiative. Plan or apply a change only when the user has asked for that change in so many words.
- To change something: call the plan tool, show the user the plan's steps, then call the apply tool with the planId and the user's request in their own words. A plan expires after 10 minutes and is used once.
- If a change is refused with ai.changes_off, the user has not allowed changes from AI tools in the app's Settings. Tell them; don't look for another way.
- Some actions are never tools: anything that sends, posts, pays, publishes, deploys or can't be undone stays a click in the app's window.
- Every error has a stable code, a message, a hint and whether retrying can work. Follow the hint.

tools.name: apply_plan
tools.description: Applies a plan from plan_change, once, if nothing it depends on changed since. Only when the user asked for this change; pass their request. Refused (ai.changes_off) unless the user allows changes from AI tools in Keeplight's Settings.

request.description: What the user asked for, in their own words.

tools.name: diagnose
tools.description: Everything for working out a problem at once, redacted: OpenRGB, the devices, the setup in counts, the settings, the keeper's last runs and the newest events. Start here for "what went wrong".

tools.name: get_devices
tools.description: Every lighting device OpenRGB reports: id, name, mode, color, whether Keeplight keeps it and as what, and what probably lights it. Also whether AI changes are allowed.

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: The newest events: every change, who made it (gui, cli or mcp:<app>), and every failure with its code.

limit.description: How many of the newest events to return; 50 when left out, at most 500.

tools.name: list_error_codes
tools.description: Every error code: what it means, what to do, whether retrying can work.

tools.name: plan_change
tools.description: Checks one change the user asked for (an action on a device) and returns a plan: its steps in plain words and a planId. Changes nothing else.

Action.description: What a change does to one device.

oneOf.description: Keep what the device shows now. Changes no light.

Keep a device whose every light is off, so it is turned back off after
sleep. Changes no light now.
Send a kept device its kept setup.

Stop keeping it; a device in Direct mode with an Onboard mode is handed
back to that, so it isn't left dark.

Keep the setup it had before the last change (stopping keeping it, or
a new color), and send it that setup. On a kept device the two swap,
so doing it twice undoes it.

Set the device to `color` and keep that. A mode that takes colors keeps
its effect in the new color; otherwise it switches to Static, or Direct.

color.description: For setColor only: the color as #rrggbb, such as "#0050ff".

device.description:
The device's id ("ram-stick-1") or display name ("RAM stick 1"), as
get_devices lists them.

zone.description:
For setColor only: one zone of the device, by its name or id as
get_devices lists its zones ("addressable-rgb-header-1"). The other
zones keep their colors. Without it, the whole device.

codes.meaning: Something else went wrong reading or writing a file.

codes.hint: Read the devices (get_devices, or keeplight-cli devices) and use an id from there.
codes.meaning: No device has that id or name.

codes.hint: Keep it first, or choose a device whose kept state is not notKept.
codes.meaning: Keeplight doesn't keep that device, so there is nothing to put back or stop keeping.

codes.hint: Only a device you stopped keeping has one (keptBefore in get_devices). Keep it instead.
codes.meaning: That device has no earlier setup to go back to.

codes.hint: Read the device's dark flag and mode, then use keep or keepDark to match.
codes.meaning: That device can't be kept the way asked: every light is off (use keepDark), or its lights aren't all off (use keep), or OpenRGB doesn't say which mode it's in.

codes.hint: Pick another device, or a color other than #000000 (use keepDark to keep a device dark). For an unknown mode, set the device in OpenRGB and keep it first.
codes.meaning: That device can't be set to that color: none of its modes takes a color, the color is black, or OpenRGB doesn't say which mode it's in, so the change couldn't be undone.

codes.hint: Read the device's zones (get_devices, or keeplight-cli devices --json) and use a zone id from there.
codes.meaning: The device has no zone with that name or id.

codes.hint: Start the OpenRGB service (or turn on its SDK server), then try again.
codes.meaning: OpenRGB isn't answering on its SDK port, so Keeplight can't see or set any light.

codes.hint: Point KEEPLIGHT_OPENRGB and KEEPLIGHT_DATA_DIR at a test server and a throwaway folder, or use the installed Keeplight.
codes.meaning: This dev or scratch run of Keeplight refused the real OpenRGB, data folder, startup entry or network.
